newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pioneer launches privatisation fund July 28.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pioneer launches privatisation fund July 28.

text.p: The Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Company will start selling units in a new fund investing in units, fund shares and firms in Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) programme, Pioneer's head said on Friday.
"(The new fund) will be an aggressive fund investing in participation units, NFI shares and shares in individual firms in the programme," Alicja Malecka told a news conference.
Fund manager Piotr Rzezniczak told the conference that 90 percent of the new fund's investment would be in bourse instruments and 10 percent in debt instruments.
He said the fund might also invest in non-public firms outside the NFI programme.
Malecka said that as a special incentive Pioneer would allow investors to pay for the fund's units with NFI participation certificates.
"Aside from cash the fund will also take NFI units. This will broaden options for people who do not want to set up investment accounts with brokers (to trade in NFI units)," she said.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme have been entitled to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which have been trading on the Warsaw bourse since June 12.
The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
